program.title: Beginner Swimming Foundation Week 1
program.goal: Build water confidence, breathing control, and basic shoulder stability for safe swimming progression

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Beginner swimmer (1 session/week, 45 min) with mild occasional shoulder discomfort post-swimming. Goals: general fitness and endurance. Needs water confidence, breathing mechanics, and shoulder durability before load progression.
primary_constraints: Mild shoulder discomfort after swimming—limit overhead volume and prioritize rotator cuff control
Beginner water confidence—focus on short repeats, recovery, and technique quality over distance
Single session per week—maximize quality and safety signaling rather than volume
sport_demands: Water confidence and breathing rhythm under fatigue—essential gate before structured sets
Scapular control and rotator cuff capacity—prevents shoulder irritation during freestyle
Trunk control and anti-extension stability—maintains body position and reduces injury risk
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Water Confidence & Shoulder Durability Foundation. Establish safe breathing, floating, and water entry/exit mechanics. Build rotator cuff and scapular stability via dry-land work. Assess 24-hour symptom response to guide next week's load.

weeks.theme: Water confidence and shoulder stability baseline

workouts.title: Pool: Water Confidence, Breathing, Shoulder Stability Prep
sport_transfer: Rhythmic breathing and face immersion reduce panic and build stroke efficiency
Scapular control and rotator cuff activation prevent shoulder strain during freestyle
Floating and streamline position lay foundation for efficient body alignment
workouts.why_this_session: Establish safe water entry/exit, rhythmic breathing, and floating before progressing volume. Rotator cuff prep reduces post-swim shoulder discomfort.

warmup.name: Pool Entry & Shallow Water Familiarization
warmup.purpose: Practice safe entry using steps or ladder, walk in waist-deep water, confirm water comfort and no panic triggers

warmup.name: Bubble Breathing Drill
warmup.purpose: Exhale bubbles through nose and mouth at wall; inhale to side. Build breath rhythm and face-immersion confidence.

warmup.name: Float and Recover
warmup.purpose: Supine or prone float holding wall, practice controlled breathing and horizontal body position awareness

main_work.name: Wall-Supported Glide & Recover
main_work.purpose: Push off wall, glide 10–15 m with body streamline, walk back, recover. Build streamline position and push-off confidence.
main_work.load_guidance: Use controlled reps in a pain-free range at the target session intensity.

main_work.name: Kick with Kickboard (Flutter)
main_work.purpose: Hold kickboard, flutter kick 15–20 m, walk back, recover. Activate legs, practice rhythmic breathing every 3–4 kicks.
main_work.load_guidance: Use controlled reps in a pain-free range at the target session intensity.

main_work.name: Stroke Practice: Bubble Breathing + Arm Movement (Supported)
main_work.purpose: In waist-deep water, practice one-arm recovery with wall support, exhale underwater, breathe to side. Limit to controlled tempo; stop if shoulder discomfort increases.
main_work.load_guidance: Use controlled reps in a pain-free range at the target session intensity.

main_work.name: Pool Exit Practice
main_work.purpose: Practice safe exit using steps or ladder, no rushing. Confirm confidence and no discomfort before leaving pool.
main_work.load_guidance: Use controlled reps in a pain-free range at the target session intensity.

cooldown.name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
cooldown.purpose: Light rotator cuff activation (1–3 lb dumbbells or bodyweight). Reduce shoulder irritation post-swim.
cooldown.load_guidance: Start with 1–2 lb dumbbell; if unavailable, use bodyweight isometric hold

cooldown.name: Inchworm Walkout
cooldown.purpose: Gentle posterior-chain and shoulder mobility refresh post-pool. Low spine load, controlled breathing.

injury_modifications: If shoulder discomfort worsens during arm work, reduce stroke repeats and focus on kicking and breathing drills instead
Avoid overhead work or pressing motions if shoulder pain is present; skip arm-recovery practice and extend water-entry familiarization time
Do external rotation only if pain-free; substitute with gentle isometric shoulder holds at neutral if discomfort appears

weeks.progression_rule: Beginner swimmers need water confidence, rhythmic breathing, and floating control before load progression. Limit to short repeats (25 m or less) with full recovery. Dry-land shoulder work 2–3× per week supports durability without pool fatigue.

program.nutrition_focus: Ensure adequate hydration before and after pool session. Focus on protein + carbohydrate within 1–2 hours post-swim to support recovery and shoulder durability.
recovery_focus: Post-swim shower to remove chlorine and reduce skin irritation
Light low-intensity movement (walking, easy stretching) on non-pool days to reduce stiffness
Monitor 24-hour shoulder response; if discomfort persists or worsens, reduce next week's stroke volume and extend recovery
Ensure 7+ hours sleep to support adaptation and reduce fatigue-driven pain flare
safety_notes: Beginner swimmers must never train unsupervised; confirm pool has lifeguard or training partner present
If breath-holding, panic, or unsafe water behavior appears, stop session immediately and reassess water confidence
Shoulder discomfort is mild and occasional; monitor post-swim soreness daily. If pain persists >24 hours or worsens, defer arm-heavy work and consult sports medicine
Do not progress to longer repeats, faster pace, or high-intensity sets until water confidence is stable (4+ weeks of safe, controlled sessions)
assumptions: Athlete has access to a pool with lifeguard and shallow end for beginner training
Mild shoulder discomfort is post-exertional and not limiting function; no structural diagnosis required to start
1 session per week is the only training day; dry-land shoulder work (external rotation, mobility) may occur on separate days if desired
Athlete can comfortably float and has no acute fear of water; water-confidence teaching progressions apply
Kickboard and pool access are guaranteed for the full week
